- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions to avoid excessive overshoot.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates; apply mild downward bias (−0.5 to −1.5%) to avoid overbought bias.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.5–0.8), model shows mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with recent 5–7 day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a 1–2% downward correction for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment drops sharply after a peak, model tends to lag; delay downward adjustment until sentiment confirms negative momentum.
- When sentiment is near 0.00 or 0.27, model often fails to recognize bearish signals; add a 1–2% downward buffer if sentiment <0.30.
- If model forecast is >10% above true for 3 consecutive days, apply a “cooling” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5% per day until convergence.
